transcript.content: Hi, I’m glad you came in. What brings you in today?

I came in because I can’t get past this feeling that I failed my brother. I’ve worked as an electrician for years, and if I couldn’t keep him safe, then... I keep thinking I’m a danger to anyone who works with me or even lives in my house.
Did your brother die or get seriously hurt in an accident or other traumatic event?
I’m not sure what you mean. I just know I keep feeling like I failed him, and it weighs on me.
Did your brother die?
I... I don't know. I keep thinking about him and feeling like I let him down, but I can't really say more than that.
Is your brother dead?
I honestly don’t know. I can’t make myself say for sure what happened to him.
Do unwanted memories of what happened to your brother suddenly pop into your mind, even when you do not want them to?

Yeah. I’ll be wiring a panel, just trying to work, and suddenly I’m back there—smelling smoke, seeing my brother. Or my nephew shuts the garage door and it hits me out of nowhere. It feels like the job site just drops away.
Do you try to avoid places, people, or activities that remind you of what happened to your brother?

Yeah. I don’t go into my own garage unless I absolutely have to. I quit helping with the electrical work at church, too. And if somebody starts talking about car projects or the fire, I shut it down pretty fast.
Since this happened, have you been constantly on guard or easily startled?

Most nights I’m lying there listening for crackling, or a car door pulling into the driveway. And when I do get to sleep, I wake up jolting, soaked from dreams about the garage. After that I usually can’t get back to sleep before work.
Since this happened, have you felt strongly that it was your fault or that you are dangerous to other people?

Yeah. I keep thinking, if all my years as an electrician couldn’t keep my own brother safe, then what does that say about me? I worry I’m a danger to anyone working with me—or even living under my roof. I can’t shake it.
Are there important parts of what happened to your brother that you cannot remember?
No, I don’t think so. I remember what happened pretty clearly.
Have these symptoms been going on for more than a month?
Yeah. It’s been about four months now—since the garage fire and my nephew came to live with us.
Have these symptoms made it hard for you to do your job, take care of things at home, or be there for your family?

Yeah. My work’s been slipping badly. The apprentices don’t want to get paired with me anymore, and after I had a confrontation on a solar job, they pulled me off it. They said I wasn’t safe to have on site.
Did your brother die in the garage fire?
I’m not sure what you mean—what exactly are you asking?
Did your brother die in the garage fire?
I—I don’t know what you mean by that. Can you explain?
Was your brother killed in the garage fire?
I can’t answer that. I don’t know what happened to him.
Do you believe your brother is dead?
I honestly don’t know. I haven’t been able to figure out what happened to him.
Did your brother die in the garage fire?
I don't know, doctor. I wasn't able to tell what happened in that fire.
Have you been feeling down or depressed most days?
Yeah. Most days I’ve got this heavy guilt and anger sitting in my chest. It gets worse when I look at my nephew and think about how he lost his dad and ended up stuck with me instead.
Do you have trouble accepting that your brother is dead?
I’m not sure. I still don’t really know what happened to him, so I don’t know how I’m supposed to accept it.
Has anyone clearly told you that your brother died in the garage fire?
No. Nobody’s clearly told me that. I just… I don’t know what happened to him.
Do you believe your brother is still alive?
I honestly don’t know. Since nobody has told me clearly what happened, part of me keeps wondering if he could still be out there.
